thread:
Alex: Heads up — pen test submitted a finding: KMS alias enumeration + an intermittent API timeout that allows a retry path to hit a legacy auth fallback. Pen marked as HIGH and attached PoC. Ticket #CS-4821.
Maria: Can you paste the PoC here or a sanitized snippet? need to triage severity.
Alex: Paste below (sanitized):
```
# discovered alias list via unauthenticated error path
GET /v1/keys HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer <invalid>

=> 403 but response included partial alias metadata for 12 keys
```
Alex: And an example of the timeout + retry chain:
```
client -> api-gateway (timeout 2s) -> retry -> legacy-auth (falls back to cached policy) -> returns 200 with limited metadata
```
Jordan: If true this could leak minimal metadata but not plaintext key material. We should confirm whether alias names or ARNs alone are in scope for high severity. My read: medium until we can show exfil of sensitive attributes.
Irene: Customer support flagged a related incident yesterday where a customer reported higher-than-normal latency and then auth flakiness. Ticket ID CS-4819 links to the same time window. Sam (support) can confirm.
Sam (support): Confirmed. Customer experienced 503s then a rush of retries. We saw ~4% elevated retries for that customer for ~12 minutes starting 2026-02-18T21:12Z.
Alex: Pen attached a CloudTrail query they used to reproduce. Sharing sanitized query: 
```
fields @timestamp, eventName, requestParameters 
| filter eventSource = "kms.amazonaws.com" and eventName = "ListAliases" and userIdentity.type = "Anonymous"
| sort @timestamp desc
```
Maria: Can we reproduce internally? Jordan: I'll take repro. Quick checklist:
- run the curl PoC against staging with the same timeout/retry
- enable debug logs on gateway
- check KMS proxy for alias response changes

Jordan: Repro steps I used (staging):
1) `curl -v -X GET "https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/keys" -H "Authorization: Bearer invalidtoken" --max-time 2`
2) Observe 403 with body including `aliases: ["alias/rdw-dev-logs", "alias/rdw-prod-svc"]`
3) Toggle gateway timeout to 1s, trigger failure -> retry path hit -> get 200 + alias list

Jordan: I can reproduce consistently on staging-legacy-route. Attaching quick logs in gist: https://gist.github.com/xxxxx (sanitized)
pen-test-bot: Automated severity suggestion: HIGH. Evidence: alias list present in response body and legacy fallback returns 200 on retry.
Maria: We need evidence of impact: are alias names considered PII or sensitive metadata per our policy? Also whether alias -> principal mapping could lead to privilege escalation.
Irene: Compliance: aliases alone are sensitive since they can reveal environment names and service roles. Policy says treat KMS metadata exposure as at least medium. High requires key material or unauthenticated ability to decrypt.
Alex: Pen argues that alias enumeration + ability to hit different endpoints via retry chain could facilitate targeted attacks. Wants high. I'm asking eng to double-check if the gateway should ever surface alias metadata on 4xx.
Jordan: Root cause is a missing filter in legacy auth path that sanitized responses earlier in the request chain. Newer path strips alias metadata on 4xx. Legacy does not.
Maria: Proposed mitigation: fast fix — patch legacy auth to mimic modern path (strip alias field on non-200). Medium-term: remove legacy fallback for unauthenticated flows, add automated test. Can we hotfix in staging and request pen to retest?
Alex: Pen asked for retest evidence (screenshots + request ids). We should provide CloudTrail proof and staging logs. Also need severity re-eval notes.
Sam (support): I'll add a support note to the customer and offer incident timeline. Also confirm we won't change prod behavior until change is validated.
Jordan: I pushed a staging patch that strips aliases on 4xx and added a unit test. Patch ID: pr/infra-2387. Deployed to staging at 2026-02-19T02:30Z. Repro steps now return 403 with empty alias array.
Jordan: How should we handoff evidence to pen for retest? I can provide: sanitized curl commands, request_ids, staging timestamps, CloudTrail query and a short recording.
Alex: That should be enough. Pen asked for evidence in 24h.
Irene: On severity: I'll propose closed-loop: keep designation at HIGH pending pen retest. If pen fails to reproduce with our staging environment and evidence, we'll drop severity to MEDIUM. Document reasoning in the finding.
Maria: Agree. Action items:
- Jordan: provide evidence bundle + replay steps to pen (due: 24h)
- Alex: update ticket CS-4821 with mitigation plan and severity rationale
- Irene: coordinate customer comms + block change to prod until signoff
- Sam: append customer incident notes linking CS-4819/CS-4821

Jordan: Evidence bundle uploaded: https://internal.redwood/safe/infra-2387-evidence.zip (access logged). Request IDs: r-20260219-001..r-20260219-025.
Alex: Thanks. Once pen confirms retest result, we'll close or adjust severity. If pen still sees alias leaks in prod path, we escalate to oncall and prepare emergency rollout.
Sam (support): Noted. I'll update the customer that we're testing a staged fix and will follow up after retest.
pen-test-bot: Retest requested. Waiting for external tester confirmation.
Alex: Closing loop here for now. Please ping if anyone hits blockers while packaging evidence. :thumbsup:
